    Prepare Data for Analysis

    PreData.Rd

    Prepares community data by removing columns, setting row names, and optionally transposing the data frame. Useful for cleaning and reformatting data before diversity analysis.

    PreData(DF, ReCols = 0, NCols = 1, transpose = FALSE)

    Arguments

    DF

    A data.frame containing community data.

    ReCols

    Integer. Number of columns to remove from the beginning of the data frame (default = 0). Useful when the first column(s) contain metadata that should be excluded.

    NCols

    Integer. Column number to use as row names (default = 1). This column will be converted to row names and then removed from the data. Special case: If NCols = 0, the function will automatically transpose the table, converting original column names into the first column (character) and the rest as numeric columns.

    transpose

    Logical. Should the data frame be transposed after processing? (default = FALSE). Only applies when NCols > 0. Ignored when NCols = 0.

    Value

    A data.frame with:

    • Row names set from the specified column (if NCols > 0)

    • Specified columns removed

    • Optionally transposed (if NCols > 0 and transpose = TRUE)

    • If NCols = 0: automatically transposed data where original column names become the first column (character) and the rest as numeric columns

    Details

    This function streamlines common data preparation tasks:

    Workflow (NCols > 0 - DEFAULT):

    1. Remove first ReCols columns (if ReCols > 0)

    2. Set row names from column NCols

    3. Remove the names column

    4. Transpose if transpose = TRUE

    Special workflow (NCols = 0):

    1. Remove first ReCols columns (if ReCols > 0)

    2. Automatically transpose the data frame excluding the first column

    3. Set column names using the first column values (species names)

    4. Add a new first column with the original column names (sample IDs)

    5. Convert the new first column to character

    6. Convert all other columns to numeric

    Note: When NCols = 0, transposition is automatic, the transpose argument is ignored.

    Common use cases:

    • Converting Excel/CSV imports to analysis-ready format

    • Handling data with multiple ID columns

    • Switching between wide and long formats

    • Preparing data for diversity functions

    • Converting species-in-columns format with proper data types

    Examples

    # Example 1: Simple case - set row names from column 1 (DEFAULT BEHAVIOR)
data_raw <- data.frame(
  Station = c("St1", "St2", "St3"),
  Capitella = c(45, 12, 3),
  Owenia = c(23, 18, 45),
  Nephtys = c(12, 34, 23)
)
PreData(data_raw, NCols = 1, transpose = FALSE)
#>     Capitella Owenia Nephtys
#> St1        45     23      12
#> St2        12     18      34
#> St3         3     45      23

# Example 2: Remove first column, use second as names, and transpose
data_raw2 <- data.frame(
  ID = 1:3,
  Station = c("St1", "St2", "St3"),
  Capitella = c(45, 12, 3),
  Owenia = c(23, 18, 45)
)
PreData(data_raw2, ReCols = 1, NCols = 1, transpose = TRUE)
#>           St1 St2 St3
#> Capitella  45  12   3
#> Owenia     23  18  45

# Example 3: Transpose without removing columns (ORIGINAL BEHAVIOR)
data_raw3 <- data.frame(
  Species = c("Capitella", "Owenia", "Nephtys"),
  St1 = c(45, 23, 12),
  St2 = c(12, 18, 34),
  St3 = c(3, 45, 23)
)
PreData(data_raw3, NCols = 1, transpose = TRUE)
#>     Capitella Owenia Nephtys
#> St1        45     23      12
#> St2        12     18      34
#> St3         3     45      23

# Example 4: NEW FEATURE - NCols = 0 auto-transposes with column names as first column
